_comment: Coordinator cadence log. One JSON object per line, append-only, no wrapping array and no trailing commas. Fields: checked_at (ISO-8601 timestamp with local UTC offset), idle (number of subagents observed idle at that instant), running (number observed running at that instant), action (what the check did with the idle capacity). Keep this file small and hand-maintained; append one line per check and never edit or delete an earlier line. This log is discipline plus visibility, never a monitor: no CI job can detect an idle agent, because a GitHub-hosted runner holds no session wall-clock and sees only the commits and workflow events it is triggered by. So nothing here is enforced automatically, and a missing entry means the check did not run, not that nothing was idle. Counts are point-in-time observations of agent state and carry no meaning once the session that produced them has ended. This log is not a work queue, not an approval grant, and not a statement that any assigned work was completed; for authority read docs/approvals/APPROVAL_REGISTER.md, and for status read the owning backlog.

_reconciliation: 2026-10-01 coordinator cadence gap. From 2026-10-01T20:22:51-07:00 through 2026-10-02T08:25:00-07:00 the coordinator recorded its cadence checks to session-local state instead of this tracked file, and session state does not survive a new chat; the coordinator's session record holds 49 checks over that window and reports 47 records lost, and neither figure is verifiable from this repository, which holds only the two entries above. The gap is a defect of the coordinator's process, not a window in which nothing ran: the checks did run, and only their records are missing, so the _comment rule that a missing entry means the check did not run does not describe this gap. No per-check record survives, and none is invented here. Recorded by the reconciliation pull request that added this line.

_cadence_rule: Appending each check to THIS tracked file is a required step of the cadence, performed at the moment of the check, not a convenience deferred to session state. This file is the record. A session log is not. A check that was not appended here cannot be told apart from one that did not run.

_correction: Correction to the _reconciliation entry on line 4 above. Its window end, 2026-10-02T08:25:00-07:00, is wrong and future-dated: the commit that added line 4 is stamped 2026-10-02 00:37:32 -07:00, hours before 08:25. The cause was the coordinator's: a UTC hour (2026-10-02T07:46Z) was stamped with the local offset -07:00, putting the value about seven hours ahead of the local time meant. The window start, 2026-10-01T20:22:51-07:00, is correct as written and verifiable from this repository: it equals the checked_at on line 3. The true end of the gap came from session state and is not derivable here, so no replacement end is invented. The 49 and 47 counts on line 4 are unaffected and remain unverifiable from this repository. Line 4 is left exactly as written; this line corrects forward. Added by the pull request that appends this line.

Correction to the _correction entry on line 6 above. Its causal clause -- that a UTC hour (2026-10-02T07:46Z) was stamped with the local offset -07:00 -- is wrong and cannot be relied on, as the coordinator recorded in a defect disclosure comment on pull request #621 on 2026-10-02. Two checkable points. First, applying that mechanism to the cited instant yields 2026-10-02T07:46:00-07:00, which is 39 minutes short of the 2026-10-02T08:25:00-07:00 actually written on line 4, so it does not reproduce the value it explains. Second, the cited instant falls after the commit that added line 4 (914dcbb8, stamped 2026-10-02 00:37:32 -07:00, which is 07:37:32Z), so it cannot be the clock reading that produced a value written before it. The cause is unrecoverable and no cause and no replacement clock reading is asserted here. What stands, and is why the line 6 correction remains warranted: line 4's window end is future-dated by 7 hours 47 minutes 28 seconds against the commit that carries it, and the magnitude line 6 states, about seven hours ahead, is correct -- only the reading cited as its source is wrong. The window start, 2026-10-01T20:22:51-07:00, still equals the checked_at on line 3. The true end of the gap is still not derivable from this repository, and the 49 and 47 counts remain unverifiable here. Lines 1 through 6 are left exactly as written; this line corrects forward. Added by the follow-up pull request that appends this line.

action: the coordinator observed the runtime's active-child limit of 15 with six further dispatches rejected, so there was zero idle capacity and no idle slot to fill. It recorded that PR #623 — the batch A governance re-read — MERGED to main as b0d3ab71 at 2026-10-03T00:01:15Z after three independent review records were posted, each bound to head 4e28afa17c86aa4be37b3c6f6b0aea29be00c956 (Audit-1 ACCEPT, REMEDY-1 SHIP, SEC-1 SECURITY-ACCEPT), with all five exact-head checks green. It verified the merge itself: exactly the three intended files changed, and the cadence log this line is being appended to still held 7 lines with the `_correction` line 7 intact — the check that would have detected a silent revert of the PR #622 correction, which did not occur. It also recorded a process flaw of its own: because it dispatched a record-posting agent without knowing another agent had already posted the security record, the security review stage is now recorded twice on PR #623 from the same identity; both records are accurate and the duplicate was left in place rather than deleted, because removing a governance record is worse than a duplicate.

the coordinator observed the bench at the runtime's then active-child cap of 8, with five agents assigned but queued for a slot, and dispatched a 13-agent roster onto two workstreams: the pull-request queue (review and merge of PR #621, a merge-readiness audit, a sweep for merged pull requests that never had an independent review posted, and a merge-readiness checklist) and the repository documentation readability acceptance backlog, grouped into three path-coherent batches (governance pages; ledger and evidence pages; about 34 skill pages plus roadmap proposals). It verified the trigger mechanism as the instruction required rather than assuming it: subagents verifiably run and report back autonomously, and a 240-second timer job fired accurately and wrote its file, but its completion notice surfaced only when the job was collected, so a background timer does NOT wake the coordinator mid-turn. It therefore recorded the honest limit that the cadence is discipline plus visibility, bounded by turns, and is never a monitor.
